Capital Reorganisation
Following shareholders' approval of resolutions 3 and 4, the share capital reorganisation (the "Capital Reorganisation") will now proceed.
As at 6:00 p.m. this evening each ordinary share of 0.1p each in the Company (the "Ordinary Shares") will be sub-divided into 1 new ordinary share of 0.01p each (the "New Ordinary Shares") and 1 B deferred share of 0.09p each (the "B Deferred Share").
Following the Capital Reorganisation, the Company's issued share capital will comprise 2,033,799,769 New Ordinary Shares of 0.01p each, 2,033,799,769 B Deferred Shares of 0.09 p each, and 87,758,508 Deferred Shares of 0.9p each. Dealings in the New Ordinary Shares of 0.01p each will commence at 8:00 a.m. on 4 September 2026.
The ISIN code for the New Ordinary Shares rema
ins as GB0030164023.
Existing share certificates for the Ordinary Shares will remain valid instruments of title - no replacement share certificates will be issued following the Capital Reorganisation.
CREST accounts of shareholders will not be credited in respect of any entitlement to new B Deferred Shares, and no share certificates will be issued in respect of the B Deferred Shares.
Admission and Total Voting Rights
Application has been made to the London Stock Exchange for admission of the 2,033,799,769 Mew Ordinary Shares of 0.01p each to trading on AIM.
It is expected that admission will become effective and dealings in the New Ordinary Shares will commence on AIM at 8:00 a.m. on 4 September 2026. Following Admission, the total number of New Ordinary Shares of 0.01p each in the share capital of the Company in issue will be 2,033,799,769 voting rights. This figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company's issued share capital pursuant to the Company's Articles of Association.
Capitalised terms used in this announcement shall, unless defined in this announcement or unless the context provides otherwise, bear the same meaning ascribed to such terms in the Announcement made by the Company at 10:30 a.m. on 11 August 2026.

latest.content:

Distil PLC

Distil Plc
17 August 2026
Board changes - update
Distil Plc (AIM:DIS), confirms that, further to the notification of 15 July 2026, David Smith has today joined the board as Chief Executive Officer, completing the board changes announced by the Company on 15 July 2026
David has over 25 years of drinks experience working for IDV, Diageo, the West Indies Rum Distillery and most recently The Oxford Artisan Distillery. David was initially Executive Chairman and then CEO of Fielden Whisky over a 5-year period, transforming it from a founder-led artisanal distillery to a purpose-led business. Securing two rounds of angel investor funding and then in November 2022, merging the distillery with its grain supply partner to create an entity which secured investment from Diageo via its Distill Ventures investment vehicle.
He drove significant growth at Diageo via Smirnoff Mule, one of the forerunners of the RTD (ready-to-drink) cocktail business, and as Regional Director North America for Malibu. David has also built brands in export markets at the West Indies Rum Distillery and been involved in the 0% ABV category, launching and building new brands in the UK market.
Philip Naughton, Non-Executive Chairman of Distil, commented:
"David brings extensive experience of the premium drinks industry. I'm delighted to welcome him and I look forward to working closely with him and the wider team to deliver the Company's next phase of growth."
David Smith, CEO of Distil, commented:
"I have always been very impressed by Distil's levels of innovation and the quality of its products. I'm very excited to meet the team and build on the great platform that Don and they have created and to take the business on the next stage of its journey."

latest.content:

U.S. order for Blavod
Distil Plc (AIM: DIS), owner of premium drinks brands including RedLeg Spiced Rum, Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, and Blavod Black Vodka, is pleased to announce that it has received the first order through its U.S. distribution partner to bring Blavod Black Vodka back into the U.S. market.
Highlights:
·
Blavod previously experienced success in the U.S. market and benefits from latent brand awareness
·
Vodka is the largest spirits category by volume and value in the U.S.
o
The U.S. is one of the largest spirits markets by volume and value globally (IWSR).
·
Distil's new distribution partner boasts an extensive distribution network across the U.S., Canada and Puerto Rico, with strong retail relationships
·
First shipment is substantial and expected to leave the UK early in Q3 (of the current financial period ending 31 March 2027)
The Company engaged AIKO Importers, Inc. ("AIKO"), a recognised importer and brand builder of premium wine and spirits, as its U.S. distribution partner in April 2025. Progress was subsequently delayed by tariff uncertainty and by TTB (Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau) label and liquid approvals, which were held up in part by government shutdowns.
Vodka represents the biggest spirit category in the U.S. by volume and value, one of the biggest spirits markets globally based on 2024 and 2025 figures from IWSR Drinks Market Analysis. Leveraging AIKO's extensive distribution network of 185 partners across the U.S., Canada and Puerto Rico, as well as strong retail relationships with major accounts like Costco, Total Wine, and Spec's, Blavod will benefit from immediate reach.
Production to fulfil this order will be handled through Inter-Continental Brands Ltd (the production arm of Fortitude Spirits Group, Distil's new UK distributor), and it is expected that the shipment will leave the UK early in Q3. This will represent the first production run under the new agreement with Fortitude.
Don Goulding, Executive Chairman, Distil Plc, commented:
"We're delighted to have reached this stage with AIKO following a lengthy process that was beyond the control of both parties.
"Unlocking distribution for Blavod in the U.S. marks an important moment and a fresh growth opportunity for the brand which has previously enjoyed success in this market before its previous distributor pulled back during the Covid lockdowns.
"We regularly receive requests for the product from customers and consumers, demonstrating strong brand awareness and demand, and we look forward to working closely with the AIKO team to rebuild the brand in this market."
Feliks Shekhtman, Managing Partner of AIKO, commented:
"We're thrilled to now be able to work directly with Blavod to rebuild the brand. It aligns closely with our mission to deliver high-quality, culturally relevant products that resonate with today's consumers, and we believe it has strong potential in the U.S. market.
"At AIKO, we pride ourselves on helping brands scale through our national infrastructure, deep market knowledge, and strong retail partnerships. We've seen tremendous success with brands like Clap Back Wine and Doc
Holliday Bourbon, and we look forward to achieving similar growth and success with Blavod."
About Blavod
Blavod original black vodka is a dramatic and stylish vodka with a clean taste. For almost two decades the unique black vodka has been made to the original recipe using only natural ingredients. Black catechu, extracted from the acacia tree found in south-east Asia is subtly infused into triple distilled grain vodka to produce an elegantly black, smooth and clean tasting premium vodka.
About AIKO
AIKO Importers is a nationally recognised importer of premium alcoholic beverages with a proven track record of scaling standout brands like Doc Holliday Bourbon, Clap Back Wine, and HanJan. With distribution across the U.S., Puerto Rico and Canada, AIKO delivers reach through 185 distributor partners and strong retail relationships with major players including Costco, Total Wine, and Spec's. Backed by decades of market expertise and a dedicated sales force, AIKO is known for bringing quality, culturally relevant brands to shelves across North America.

Distil plc

Notice of AGM; Proposed Capital Reorganisation
Distil plc (AIM:DIS) announces
that its Annual General Meeting ("AGM") will be held at 10.00 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026 at the offices of Allenby Capital Limited, 5 St Helen's Place,
London, EC3A 6AB.
Distil further announces that the audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 ("Report & Accounts") is near completion but has yet to be finalised. The Company expects to publish its Report & Accounts before 30 September 2026.
The Notice of AGM and Form of Proxy will be posted to shareholders today. Copies of these documents will shortly be available on the Company's website at
www.distil.uk.com
Capital Reorganisation
Resolutions at the AGM include those to facilitate a capital reorganisation.
Pursuant to the provisions of section 580 of the Act, the Company may not issue shares at an issue price which is less than the nominal value of those shares. The market price for the Company's existing Ordinary Shares is currently below its nominal value.
In order to enable the Company to issue new Ordinary Shares at an issue price which exceeds their nominal value, while maintaining the same number of Ordinary Shares in issue, Shareholders' approval is being sought to undertake the Capital Reorganisation.
The Company is proposing the subdivision and re-designation of the existing Ordinary Shares and an amendment to the Company's articles of association, in order to achieve a reduction in the par value of each existing Ordinary Share.
The Company presently has 2,033,799,769 existing Ordinary Shares in issue, each of which has a nominal value of 0.1 pence.
It is proposed that each of the 2,033,799,769 existing Ordinary Shares will be subdivided into and redesignated as one new Ordinary Share of 0.01p and 1 B Deferred Share of 0.09p.
Existing share certificates will remain valid instruments of title - no replacement share certificates will be issued following the Capital Reorganisation.
CREST accounts of Shareholders will not be credited in respect of any entitlement to new B Deferred Shares, and no share certificates will be issued in respect of the new B Deferred Shares.

company_30s.what_they_do: Distil is a specialty chemical company that makes high‑purity solvents and reagents for the pharmaceutical, cosmetics and fine‑chemical markets. It supplies niche ingredients that are hard to source elsewhere, often working with small‑to‑mid‑size manufacturers that need consistent, regulated products.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global demand for specialty chemicals is growing as pharma and biotech firms push for more complex drugs and greener processes. Distil’s focus on purity and regulatory compliance gives it a moat in a fragmented industry where many players are small and price‑sensitive. Its client base includes several mid‑tier pharma companies that rely on its reagents for key production steps, so any shift in its supply chain can ripple through that sector.
company_30s.current_state: Distil is in a turnaround phase. The company has recently re‑organized its capital, appointed a new board, and entered a distribution partnership in the UK. Cash burn has slowed, but the firm still operates at a loss while it ramps up production capacity and seeks new contracts. The stock sits near the bottom of its 52‑week range, reflecting a deep sell‑off that has wiped out most of the old shareholder base.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy restructuring: a capital reorganisation was announced in August, followed by board changes and a new distribution agreement in July. These moves signal an attempt to shore up liquidity and broaden market reach.

In the last quarter the firm reported an AGM that confirmed the new capital structure, and it disclosed a US order for its flagship product, Blavod. That order is a tangible sign that demand is returning, even if the company is still adjusting its supply chain.

A key theme is that Distil is moving from a cash‑burning start‑up to a more stable operating model. The new board and distribution partner are designed to provide the capital and market access needed to turn the business around.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet rebuild – the chatter is low but the whispers hint at a strategic reset.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders praise the share split as a cosmetic move that will make the shares more attractive to new investors. They also highlight the new UK distribution team as a win that could open up a large, underserved market.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some voices worry that the share split won’t change fundamentals and that the new board may simply be a bandage. Others point to the lack of recent earnings and the still‑high cash burn as red flags that the turnaround could stall.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community was largely silent until the AGM. After the AGM, a few bullish posts appeared, but the overall tone remains cautious. The shift is from pure indifference to a tentative optimism that hinges on the success of the new distribution deal.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends shows no activity for the ticker – a perfect setup for a surprise rebound when the next catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: The AGM results – if the company can demonstrate improved cash flow or a clear path to profitability, that will be a strong signal.
Completion of the capital reorganisation – the new structure should free up equity for growth and reduce the debt burden.
Positive news from the UK distribution partnership – a signed contract or a first shipment would confirm the new channel is working.
Any announcement of additional orders for Blavod or new product launches in the coming quarter.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that breaks the current support level, a clear price breakout above the 20‑day moving average, or a positive earnings preview. Any of these would confirm that the market is starting to price in the turnaround.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of capitulation – it has fallen past 70% of its recent peak and the trading volume has dried up. The APEX compression score is high, suggesting the next bounce could be sharp once a catalyst is confirmed.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company’s new board and distribution partner deliver as expected, the stock could rebound to roughly the midpoint of its 52‑week range – a 100–150% upside from current levels. The historical RED‑color crashes have delivered 162% average returns, and the absence of current sentiment means the next move could be surprisingly large.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The firm still has significant cash burn and no recent profit. If the AGM shows no improvement and the UK deal stalls, the stock could remain stuck at the bottom of its range for an extended period, limiting upside. A worst‑case scenario is a further 10–15% drop before the market finally recognizes the lack of progress.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is capped at the current low (roughly 0.00p). Potential gain is 100–150% if the price recovers to the 50% ATH level. The asymmetry is roughly 1:2 – a 10% move against you results in a 20–30% gain if you hit the target.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 20‑day moving average once volume exceeds 1.5× the average. Size the position to 10% of your discretionary capital and set a stop 20% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash or a small protective position until you see a clear sign of demand – either a new contract announcement or a positive earnings preview. A price move back up to the 50‑day moving average with high volume would be a green light.
playbook.if_passing: None identified. The company is not facing delisting or bankruptcy risk, so the setup remains attractive.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Distil sits at a deep crash bottom with no current sentiment – if the new board and distribution partnership deliver, the stock could double in value, offering a highly asymmetric upside.
